vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who visits a place for fun
vocabulary.example: Many tourists visit the old city in summer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a nation with its own land and government
vocabulary.example: Egypt is a country in Africa.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a meeting where one person asks another person questions
vocabulary.example: The reporter has an interview with the teacher.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who finds and tells the news
vocabulary.example: Anna is a reporter for The News.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the country you belong to as a citizen
vocabulary.example: What is your nationality? - I'm Jordanian.

vocabulary.meaning_en: from Bangladesh
vocabulary.example: Sabrina is Bangladeshi.

vocabulary.meaning_en: from China; the language of China
vocabulary.example: Louis speaks Chinese and English.

vocabulary.meaning_en: from Iran
vocabulary.example: Mehrnoush is Iranian.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the main language of Iran (also called Persian)
vocabulary.note_ar: Farsi و Persian اسمان للغة نفسها.
vocabulary.note_en: Farsi and Persian are the same language.
vocabulary.example: People in Iran speak Farsi.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the words people use to speak and write
vocabulary.example: Arabic is a beautiful language.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say words; to use a language
vocabulary.note_ar: نقول speak English وليس speak in English عند ذكر اللغة التي نعرفها
vocabulary.example: I speak Arabic and a little English.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the study of things that happened in the past
vocabulary.example: I like history. I read about old cities.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building or statue made to remember a person or event
vocabulary.example: The Washington Monument is very tall.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place or thing that helps people remember someone
vocabulary.example: The Lincoln Memorial is beautiful.

vocabulary.meaning_en: living; not dead
vocabulary.note_ar: come alive = يدبّ فيه الحياة / يصبح حيًّا
vocabulary.note_en: come alive = become real and interesting
vocabulary.example: Old photos make history come alive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the one you like the most
vocabulary.example: Which is your favorite museum?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where you can see art or old and interesting things
vocabulary.example: We visit the science museum on Friday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: paintings, drawings and other beautiful things people make
vocabulary.example: She likes the art museum.

vocabulary.meaning_en: costing no money
vocabulary.note_ar: free لها معنى آخر: غير مشغول
vocabulary.example: The museum is free on Sundays.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the group of people who control a country
vocabulary.note_ar: حرف n لا يُنطق بوضوح غالبًا: /ˈɡʌvərmənt/
vocabulary.note_en: The first n is often silent.
vocabulary.example: The government builds new schools.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the work and ideas of government
vocabulary.example: My uncle reads about politics every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who works in government or politics
vocabulary.example: Washington has many politicians.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the building where lawmakers meet (the U.S. Capitol)
vocabulary.note_en: Do not confuse with capital (the main city).
vocabulary.example: The U.S. Capitol is in Washington, D.C.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a fun ride with toy horses that go round and round
vocabulary.example: The children ride the carousel in the park.

vocabulary.meaning_en: two, or a small number of
vocabulary.example: Can I ask you a couple of questions?

fine_lines.title: country vs nationality vs language
fine_lines.explanation_ar: اسم البلد غير اسم الجنسية واسم اللغة أحيانًا: China (البلد) / Chinese (الجنسية واللغة). Iran (البلد) / Iranian (الجنسية) / Farsi (اللغة). نقول: I'm from + بلد، و I'm + جنسية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: The country name is often different from the nationality and the language: China / Chinese; Iran / Iranian / Farsi. Say: I'm from + country, and I'm + nationality.

examples.sentence: He is Chinese. He speaks Chinese.

fine_lines.title: capital vs capitol
fine_lines.explanation_ar: capital = العاصمة (المدينة الرئيسية في البلد). Capitol = مبنى الكونغرس في واشنطن. النطق متشابه جدًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A capital is the main city of a country. The Capitol is the building where U.S. lawmakers meet. They sound almost the same.

examples.sentence: Cairo is the capital of Egypt.
She wants to see the U.S. Capitol.

fine_lines.title: What vs Which
fine_lines.explanation_ar: what للسؤال العام بلا خيارات محددة. which عندما نختار من مجموعة محددة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use what for an open question. Use which when you choose from a small group.

examples.sentence: Which is your favorite: the museum or the park?

expressions.phrase: Do you have time for an interview?
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask someone to answer some questions.
expressions.example: Excuse me, do you have time for an interview?
Can you help me? - Sure, I have time.
What is your name? - My name is Omar.
What country are you from? - I'm from Morocco.
Where are you from? - I'm from Jordan.
What languages do you speak? - Arabic and English.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking which one someone likes most.
expressions.example: We have tea and coffee. Which is your favorite?

expressions.meaning_en: A polite thank-you after someone helps or talks with you.
expressions.example: Thank you for your time, sir.
Thanks for your help! - You're very welcome.
You're going to the park? Have fun!

expressions.meaning_ar: وها هو ذا / هذا كل شيء.
expressions.meaning_en: Used at the end to say 'that is the information'.
expressions.example: There you have it: three easy ways to learn new words.

grammar.title: Questions with be: Where are you from?
grammar.explanation_ar: 1) سؤال بأداة استفهام: Wh + be + فاعل: Where are you from? / What is your name? 2) سؤال نعم/لا: نقدّم be على الفاعل: Are you from Washington? والجواب: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
grammar.explanation_en: 1) Wh- question: question word + be + subject: Where are you from? What is your name? 2) Yes/no question: put be before the subject: Are you from Washington? Answer: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
examples: Where is she from? - She's from Iran.
Are you from China? - Yes, I am.
Is he Bangladeshi? - No, he isn't. He's Indian.

grammar.title: Questions with do: What do you like?
grammar.explanation_ar: مع الأفعال العادية (like, speak) نستخدم do في السؤال: Wh + do + فاعل + فعل. What do you like to do? / What languages do you speak? وسؤال نعم/لا: Do you like Washington? - Yes, I do.
grammar.explanation_en: With normal verbs (like, speak), use do: question word + do + subject + verb. What languages do you speak? Yes/no: Do you like Washington? - Yes, I do.
examples: What do you like about the city?
What languages do you speak? - I speak Arabic and English.
Do you like museums? - Yes, I do.

grammar.title: like + verb-ing
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد like نستطيع أن نضع فعلًا ينتهي بـ ing لنقول ماذا نحب أن نفعل: I like walking. / She likes learning about history.
grammar.explanation_en: After like, you can use a verb with -ing to talk about activities you enjoy: I like walking. She likes learning about history.
examples: I like walking around the city.

questions.question: Louis is from China. He is ___.
questions.explanation_en: The nationality for China is Chinese.

questions.question: What language do people speak in Iran?
Where ___ you from?
questions.explanation_ar: مع you نستخدم are: Where are you from?
questions.explanation_en: With you, use are: Where are you from?

questions.question: What languages ___ you speak?
questions.explanation_ar: speak فعل عادي، فنستخدم do في السؤال.
questions.explanation_en: Speak is a normal verb, so we use do.

questions.question: A person who visits a place for fun is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A tourist visits places for fun.

questions.question: 'Are you from Washington, D.C.?' - 'No, ___.'
questions.explanation_ar: السؤال بـ are فالجواب المنفي: No, I'm not.
questions.explanation_en: A question with are has the short answer No, I'm not.

questions.question: Many museums in D.C. are free. 'Free' here means:
questions.explanation_en: Here free means it costs no money.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I like walk around the city.
I like walking around the city.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد like نضع فعلًا بـ ing، ومع I نقول like بدون s.
questions.explanation_en: Use like + verb-ing; with I, like has no -s.

questions.question: The main city of a country is the ___.
questions.explanation_ar: capital هي العاصمة. Capitol مبنى الكونغرس.
questions.explanation_en: Capital is the main city; the Capitol is a building.

questions.question: 'Thank you for your time.' - Best answer:
questions.explanation_ar: نرد على الشكر بـ You're very welcome.
questions.explanation_en: We answer thank you with You're very welcome.
